name: Yasukazu Tanaka
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for the Japan national football team on January 2, 1955 at age 21, playing 4 international matches that year.
early_history_summary: Tanaka played football at Hiroshima Kokutaiji High School and then Chuo University in Tokyo. As a university student, he debuted for the Japan national team against Burma on January 2, 1955, and earned 4 caps that year. He also reached the runner-up spot at the 1955 Emperor's Cup with Chuo University teammates including Ken Naganuma and Masao Uchino.

evidence_summary: Tanaka rose through the Japanese university football system, playing at Chuo University alongside future national team players like Ken Naganuma and Masao Uchino. His selection for the Japan national team in 1955 at age 21 represents a material milestone achieved through the university-to-national-team pipeline. No family background or financial information is documented in available sources. Growing up in post-war Japan likely created significant adversity but also opportunity through institutional sports programs.
starting_point: Born in 1933 in the Empire of Japan; attended Hiroshima Kokutaiji High School before enrolling at Chuo University in Tokyo.
current_position: Former Japanese footballer; believed to be living in retirement in Japan as of 2025.

name: Mina
milestone_by_age_26: Released 'Tintarella di luna' in September 1959 at age 19, reaching #3 on Italian charts with 200,000 copies sold; followed by first #1 hit 'Il cielo in una stanza' in 1960 at age 20.
early_history_summary: Mina began performing in 1958 at age 18 with the band Happy Boys in small clubs near Cremona, Italy. She was discovered by Italdisc producer David Matalon, who recorded her first singles. Her loud syncopated rendition of 'Nessuno' on national TV in early 1959 made her a sensation, and by 1960 she had her first #1 single and performed at the Sanremo Festival.
family_context_summary: Born in Busto Arsizio, Lombardy to a middle-class family; her family initially resisted her music career, refusing to let her skip college for a tour of Turkey.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family musical background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: live performance immersion,TV exposure,exceptional vocal range,Italian postwar cultural boom,producer discovery
evidence_summary: Mina emerged from a middle-class family in Busto Arsizio with no documented musical lineage. She began performing at 18 in small clubs and was discovered by Italdisc producer David Matalon, who recorded her first singles. Her exceptional three-octave soprano voice and distinctive 'urlo' singing style set her apart immediately. She leveraged Italy's post-war TV expansion and economic boom, appearing on RAI programs like Lascia o raddoppia? in 1959. Her family resisted her career, refusing to let her skip college, which created friction but also urgency. By age 20 she had a #1 single and Sanremo Festival appearance.
starting_point: Born in 1940 in Busto Arsizio, Lombardy, Italy to a middle-class family; father Giacomo and mother Regina.
current_position: Retired from public performances since 1978 but continues releasing music from Switzerland; one of the best-selling Italian artists of all time with over 1,500 songs recorded.

Achieved #1 hit in West Germany with 'Heißer Sand' and embarked on international television and concert tours.
Hosted RAI's Studio Uno, becoming Italy's most prominent television variety star.
Retired from public performances and television appearances, continuing to release albums privately.
Released single 'Un briciolo di allegria' featuring Blanco, debuting at #1 on Italian charts.

name: Brett Hull
milestone_by_age_26: Scored 72 goals in the 1989-90 NHL season at age 25 and won the Lady Byng Memorial Trophy, becoming one of the most prolific goal-scorers in NHL history.
early_history_summary: Brett Hull grew up immersed in hockey as the son of NHL legend Bobby Hull and professional figure skater Joanne McKay. He started organized hockey at age 4 in Chicago and played in the 1977 Quebec Pee-Wee tournament. Despite being overlooked as a 'pudgy' youth, he scored 105 goals in 56 games for the Penticton Knights (BCJHL) and earned a scholarship to University of Minnesota-Duluth. Drafted 117th overall by Calgary in 1984, he split time between Calgary and the minors before being traded to St. Louis in 1988, where he broke out with 41 goals his first season and 72 the next.
family_context_summary: Born to Bobby Hull (NHL Hall of Famer) and Joanne McKay (American professional figure skater); grew up in an affluent hockey household with three brothers who also played professional sports. Parents divorced acrimoniously in 1979.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Bobby Hull was one of the greatest NHL players of his era; mother was a professional figure skater who taught Brett to skate; uncle Dennis Hull was also a longtime NHL player. Brett skated with the Chicago Black Hawks as a child.
primary_early_advantage_tags: NHL father,figure skater mother,hockey culture immersion,early skating,parents divorce,underdog motivation
evidence_summary: Brett Hull was born into one of hockey's most prominent families: his father Bobby Hull was an NHL legend and his mother Joanne McKay was a professional figure skater. He started skating at age 4, had access to NHL facilities and players as a child, and grew up fully immersed in professional hockey culture. Despite these advantages, he was initially overlooked as overweight and unmotivated, drafted only 117th overall. His parents' bitter divorce in 1979 and estrangement from his father may have created additional motivation. He developed into one of the greatest goal-scorers in NHL history through a combination of family-domain knowledge and elite shooting skill.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Belleville, Ontario to Bobby Hull (NHL Hall of Fame winger) and Joanne McKay (professional figure skater); grew up in an affluent hockey household in Chicago and Winnipeg.
current_position: Executive vice president of the St. Louis Blues; retired from playing in 2005 with 741 career NHL goals (5th all-time) and two Stanley Cups.

name: Ofra Haza
milestone_by_age_26: Named Singer of the Year in Israel in 1980 at age 22, the first of four consecutive years; her first hit 'Ga'agu'im' reached #1 on the Israeli hit parade in 1974 at age 16.
early_history_summary: Ofra Haza grew up in Tel Aviv's impoverished Hatikvah Quarter as the youngest of nine children in a Yemeni Jewish immigrant family. Her mother, a singer in Yemen, taught her traditional Yemenite songs. At age 12, she joined the Hatikvah Quarter Theater Workshop led by Bezalel Aloni, who became her lifelong manager and mentor. Her song 'Ga'agu'im' reached #1 on the Israeli hit parade around 1973-74 when she was 16. After army service, she launched her solo career, with 'Shir ha-Freha' (1979) becoming a massive hit and earning her Singer of the Year honors from 1980 to 1983.
family_context_summary: Born to Yemeni Jewish immigrant parents in Tel Aviv's impoverished Hatikvah Quarter; youngest of nine children; mother Shoshana was a professional singer in Yemen who taught Ofra traditional Yemenite songs.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a professional singer in Yemen who performed at family celebrations and transmitted traditional Yemenite musical knowledge to Ofra from an early age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mentor Bezalel Aloni,Yemenite musical heritage,poverty,Hatikvah Quarter Theater Workshop,early performing,Israeli hit parade
evidence_summary: Ofra Haza was born into poverty in Tel Aviv's Hatikvah Quarter to Yemeni Jewish immigrants, the youngest of nine children. Her mother, a singer in Yemen, transmitted traditional Yemenite songs that became the foundation of Ofra's distinctive musical style. At age 12, she was discovered by Bezalel Aloni, who ran the Hatikvah Quarter Theater Workshop and became her sustained mentor and manager, providing voice training, dance lessons, and career guidance. Her first hit at age 16 and four consecutive Singer of the Year awards (1980-1983) demonstrate how mentorship, cultural heritage, and early performing opportunities combined to create a breakthrough despite severe economic disadvantage.
starting_point: Born in 1957 in Tel Aviv's impoverished Hatikvah Quarter to Yemeni Jewish immigrant parents; mother was a singer in Yemen, father Yefet worked modestly; youngest of nine children.
current_position: Died February 23, 2000 at age 42 from AIDS-related organ failure in Ramat Gan, Israel; final major work was voicing Yochevet in The Prince of Egypt (1998).

Died on February 23, 2000 from AIDS-related organ failure in Ramat Gan.

name: Vyacheslav Zudov
milestone_by_age_26: Selected into the Soviet cosmonaut corps on October 23, 1965 at age 23, completing cosmonaut training by December 1967 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Vyacheslav Zudov was born in Bor, Russian SFSR and graduated from high school in Elektrostal near Moscow. He attended the Higher Military Pilot School in Balashov, graduating in 1963 as a military transport aviation pilot. He served as a co-pilot on An-12 transport aircraft before being selected into the Soviet cosmonaut corps in October 1965 as part of Air Force Group 3. He completed cosmonaut training by December 1967 and served as backup and support crew for several Almaz space station missions before commanding Soyuz 23 in 1976.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet military pilot school,cosmonaut selection,Space Race,An-12 transport pilot,cosmonaut cohort
evidence_summary: Zudov's path to becoming a cosmonaut ran through the highly selective Soviet military aviation pipeline. He graduated from the Higher Military Pilot School in Balashov in 1963 and served as a military transport pilot before being selected for cosmonaut training in 1965 at age 23. The Soviet space program was at the height of the Space Race, making cosmonaut selection one of the most competitive and elite pipelines in the world. No family background information is available in reviewed sources. His cosmonaut cohort, including crewmate Valery Rozhdestvensky, provided a high-trust peer environment.
starting_point: Born in 1942 in Bor, Nizhny Novgorod region, Soviet Union; graduated from high school in Elektrostal near Moscow before entering military pilot training.
current_position: Died June 12, 2024 at age 82; final role was retired cosmonaut (retired May 1987), later worked in commercial science and Russian customs.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Higher Military Pilot School in Balashov as a military transport aviation pilot.

Died on June 12 and was buried in the Federal Military Memorial Cemetery in Moscow.
